title: Industry Pulse — AI / Agent Ecosystem

bullets.title: Moonshot ships Kimi K3 — a 2.8T open-weight model that takes #1 on Frontend Code Arena, beating Claude Fable 5
bullets.summary: Announced Jul 16 and covered by Bloomberg Jul 17, Kimi K3 is a 2.8-trillion-parameter Mixture-of-Experts model (896 experts, 16 active per token) on Kimi Delta Attention, with native vision and a 1M-token context. It placed #1 on Arena's Frontend Code Arena — a 17-place jump from K2.6 — winning six of seven frontend domains, with self-reported scores including 88.3 Terminal-Bench 2.1 and 81.2 FrontierSWE. Moonshot's own table has it beating Claude Opus 4.8 max and GPT-5.5 high while losing to Claude Fable 5 and GPT-5.6 Sol. Open weights are promised by July 27, 2026.
bullets.how: The load-bearing fact is the Jul 27 open-weight drop, not the leaderboard. A frontier-adjacent model we can run on our own infrastructure at zero per-token cost is directly relevant to high-volume Construct jobs and to the frontend/site work behind Brand 9 Signs, where '#1 on Frontend Code Arena' is the exact axis that matters. Self-reported vendor benchmarks are a claim, not a result — flag Jul 27, read the license, and bench one real B9S frontend task before it earns a slot in the fleet.

bullets.title: Claude Code's Jul 17 release adds an installation-health check that finds unused skills, MCP servers, and plugins versus their context cost
bullets.summary: The July 17, 2026 update adds a health pass that inspects installation state, flags unused skills / MCP servers / plugins against the context they cost, deduplicates local CLAUDE.md files against checked-in ones, proposes trimming CLAUDE.md content the model could derive from the codebase, and flags slow hooks — alongside the earlier v2.1.212 changes (2-minute MCP auto-background, /resume session picker). Provenance caveat: GitHub's releases page served a stale cache this fire, so the exact version tag carrying this feature is not independently confirmed here; the feature description is from the aggregator.
bullets.how: This is a governance tool aimed squarely at the problem The Construct keeps naming in its own praxis lessons: a fleet of skills, plugins, and MCP servers whose context cost nobody has audited. It is also the right instrument for the MCP-migration inventory the Jul 28 spec deadline demands — run the health pass across the fleet, and the 'unused MCP server' list and the 'servers that break on Jul 28' list should be reconciled in the same sitting. Verify the version tag on the primary release page before quoting one.

bullets.title: MCP specification 2026-07-28 goes final in 10 days — the largest breaking revision since launch
bullets.summary: From the maintainers' own post: the RC locked May 21 and the final spec publishes July 28. The core goes stateless — the initialize/initialized handshake and Mcp-Session-Id header are removed (SEP-2575, SEP-2567), with protocol version and client info moving into _meta; Streamable HTTP now requires Mcp-Method and Mcp-Name headers; Extensions become first-class with MCP Apps and a reshaped Tasks extension (anyone on the 2025-11-25 experimental Tasks API must migrate); Roots, Sampling, and Logging are deprecated annotation-only with a 12-month floor; tool schemas lift to full JSON Schema 2020-12; and the missing-resource error moves from MCP-custom -32002 to standard -32602.
bullets.how: Every MCP server The Construct runs sits on the far side of a breaking change in 10 days. Two concrete exposures remain: any code matching the literal -32002, and any skill assuming session-scoped state the transport will no longer carry. Pair this with the Jul 17 install-health pass — the same tool that lists unused servers should be the vehicle for the migration inventory. Do it this week, not on Jul 29.

bullets.title: Ode with Anthropic — the funded, PE-backed AI-services firm sitting directly on PRAGMA's wedge (Jul 15, carried)
bullets.summary: Three days on, nothing has moved the read: Ode is a standalone company built on Fractional AI (acquired May 2026), combining Anthropic's models with a team of engineers and operators, backed by Blackstone, Hellman & Friedman, Goldman Sachs, General Atlantic, Apollo, GIC, and Sequoia, targeting 'midsize enterprises looking to move beyond AI pilots and embed the technology into day-to-day operations.'
bullets.how: That is PRAGMA's positioning written by someone else with a private-equity consortium behind it. Carried because it is still the item that matters strategically and the question it forces is still unanswered in specifics: what is PRAGMA that Ode structurally cannot be? The candidates — we operate inside the client's owned stack, we take engagements Ode's economics won't, we're model-agnostic where Ode is definitionally not — remain untested. Continuity, not news; stays on the board until the answer exists in specifics.

praxis_lesson: The two freshest items on today's board — Kimi K3 and the Claude Code health pass — pull in opposite directions and both are about provenance, the axis this scan keeps failing on. K3 arrives wrapped in self-reported benchmarks that beat Claude Fable 5; the discipline is to record the one verifiable, dated fact (open weights Jul 27) and treat the leaderboard as an unverified vendor claim until we run it ourselves. The health pass arrives with a real, specific, dated feature but a version tag I could not confirm because GitHub served a stale cache — so I reported the feature and flagged the gap rather than inventing a tag, which is the Jul 15 error run in reverse. The through-line is the one three fires have now written down: a claim is not a result, and the fix for a provenance gap is to name it, not paper over it. The action that ties the day together is concrete — pair the install-health pass with the MCP deadline and run one pass that produces both the unused-server list and the Jul-28 migration inventory before the deadline.
